parsed.explanation: Thin-data dossier; I extrapolated from structural signals. Sections 430/431 remain in force with custodial penalties, but a 2023 government report says they are not enforced, and no trans-specific offence, police targeting or trans-specific violence is documented, so the statutes are a secondary signal. The main exposures are the absence of legal gender recognition, so a visitor's birth-sex-marked documents cannot be corrected; the absence of any anti-discrimination or harassment law; documented discrimination in services (LGBTIQ-wide, not trans-specific); and fear of prosecution deterring reporting to police, which removes recourse for visitors too. Border and document practice, custody placement and healthcare access are unevidenced, so these are open questions rather than established exposures. No documented social acceptance of gender diversity offsets this. Overall: elevated risk, toward the lower end of the band.
